chunk_findings.detail: The committed-log comparison is disabled for the entire commit whenever any exported document is staged, reverting that commit to the live-shard comparison that the bug is about. The bug report names two artifacts whose commit is refused: "a generated view (rule file, **DDFLOW.md**)". Given that rule files are TOML (per [D-rules-format]) and `exports` is the dict of documents regenerated by `ddflow export`, DDFLOW.md is an export, so `committed is None` for exactly the commit the bug describes and `return _verdict(mode, probe_lines)` is taken — a DDFLOW.md commit is still refused with "the event log it is rendered from has N change(s) the commit does not record" while another agent appends. The exclusion is also not per-file: a commit that stages a rule file *together with* a re-rendered export (the normal output of a re-render) loses the fix for the rule file too, since `exports` is non-empty. The stated regression test only covers "stage a rule file" with no export staged, so it cannot detect this. Either the export case must be compared against the committed log as well (the export is rendered from the log, so the same reasoning applies — the only difference is the size of the window), or the refusal must be scoped per staged file rather than disabling the whole check.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py → `_committed_log_if_unrecorded` (`if exports: return None`)

chunk_findings.detail: When the staged view genuinely disagrees with the committed log, the `err`/`lines` produced by `_disagreements(repo, committed, ...)` are thrown away and the user is shown `probe_lines` instead. Concretely: a rule file re-rendered from events that are not in the commit (a real staleness, not a race) plus one shard another agent has appended to yields `err`/`lines` non-empty, and the reported reason becomes "the event log … is not fully staged", with the remedy `git add <all staged|exports|rules>` — i.e. the user is told to stage the live shards, which is the opposite of the fix's intent; after doing so the check merely re-runs and produces the real message. The refusal itself is still correct, so this is diagnostics only, but it is the failure mode that made the original bug so hard to diagnose (the reported loop of commit/merge/commit), and the cause is that the committed-log branch discards `err`/`lines` in favour of the probe text.

chunk_findings.detail: The helper's contract is "or None to keep the disk's [comparison]", but the only caller turns `None` into `return _verdict(mode, probe_lines)` — a refusal — and never runs the disk comparison (`_disagreements(repo, log, …)`) it promised to fall back to. `None` is returned whenever `exports` is non-empty, i.e. for any commit that stages an exported document. So a commit that stages an export (the report itself names DDFLOW.md as one of the two views that get refused: "a generated view (rule file, DDFLOW.md)") plus a rule file takes exactly the pre-fix path: with another agent appending a shard, `exports` is truthy, `probe_lines` is non-empty, and the caller returns the original "the event log it is rendered from has N change(s) the commit does not record" refusal without ever comparing against the committed log. The docstring's justification ("an exported document is regenerated from the live log") is the very race the commit message says the fix removes, so the fix is incomplete for the class of views the bug names; the new committed-log comparison is only reachable when the commit happens to contain no export at all.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/services/enforce.py:1560 (`_committed_log_if_unrecorded`) / the new `if probe_lines:` branch

chunk_findings.detail: When the comparison against the committed log does fail (`err or lines`), the code discards `err`/`lines` and returns `_verdict(mode, probe_lines)`, whose text is "the log … is not fully staged" plus the remedy `git add <staged ∪ exports ∪ rules>`. Given a stale view (rendered from older events) plus one unstaged shard another agent is writing, the user is instructed to `git add` the shard, which stages that agent's in-flight events into this commit — the opposite of what the fix is for — and the retry then fails with a different message ("the event log it is rendered from …"), so the first refusal misdirects. `err`/`lines` are already computed and should be what is reported.

chunk_findings.detail: `git ls-files -- rel_dir` returning an empty list (no `.jsonl` tracked under the log dir in the index) is turned into `CommittedLog(log_dir, [])` — i.e. "the committed log is empty" — instead of `None`, which is the helper's documented "git cannot say, the caller keeps its refusal" value. The docstring states the invariant explicitly ("None is never read as an empty log: the caller keeps its refusal"), which shows the caller *does* distinguish "empty log" (nothing to compare, so nothing is unrecorded) from "undeterminable log" (refuse). The empty-`names` path reaches the dangerous case without any git error, so the guard is bypassed by a different route. Concrete input: the worktree/branch scenario from the bug report where `.ddflow/events` shards are not committed in this checkout (the reporter had to copy the primary's shards into the worktree) — `git ls-files -- .ddflow/events` prints nothing, `committed_log` returns a 0-event log, the comparison finds no change the staged view fails to record, and a stale or hand-edited `DDFLOW.md`/rule file is accepted under `[enforce].generated_views = block`, where the old working-tree read refused it. The fix is to return `None` when the listing is empty (or when the pathspec matched nothing), exactly as the docstring promises.
